subjects.displayTitle: Pride and vanity: when the self obscures the gift
subjects.introduction: Bahá’u’lláh describes a man who seats himself among the sandals by the door while coveting in his heart the seat of honour, and asks him what manner of person pretends to be other than he is. Pride wears many garments. It can be sewn from learning, from wealth or lineage, from office, from closeness to holy persons, even from religion itself; it can even parade as modesty. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá warns that the moment someone feels an atom superior to another, decline has begun, and that whoever says “I am perfect” has stopped growing. The remedy is not self-contempt, since man is noble and the sign of God is in all things, but honest search for one’s own faults, forgiveness of others, and work that needs no applause. The two prayers in Luke, the Pharisee’s and the publican’s, put the same choice in a few lines [1]. From here the way leads toward humility and lowliness, the emptiness of learning that forgets its source, and false claims to spiritual station.
subjects.arc: Begin with humility’s possible disguise, examine the many forms of self-exaltation, and turn toward gratitude, honest learning, and unostentatious service.

order.why: Open with outward modesty that conceals a desire for honor.
shortened: Amongst the people is he who seateth himself amid the sandals by the door whilst coveting in his heart the seat of honour. Say: What manner of man art thou, O vain and heedless one, who wouldst appear as other than thou art? And among the people is he who layeth claim to inner knowledge, and still deeper knowledge concealed within this knowledge. Say: Thou speakest false! By God! What thou dost possess is naught but husks which We have left to thee as bones are left to dogs.
Wish not for others what ye wish not for yourselves; fear God, and be not of the prideful.

order.why: Distinguish human nobility from considering oneself superior.
shortened: Indeed, man is noble, for within all things the sign of God exists, but to regard oneself as more learned, superior, more excellent, more God-fearing and more exalted is a grievous error.

order.why: Join learning and righteousness with forgiveness rather than contempt.
Direct scrutiny toward one’s own shortcomings.
Retain the related counsel as a separate source.
shortened: One must always search for his own shortcomings so that he may repent at the threshold of Oneness and become protected and guarded; otherwise, pride and haughtiness will take possession of one's heart and this will cause deprivation of the bounties of the Court of Singleness.

order.why: Read the reported warning that claiming perfection can stop growth.
shortened: I beg of God that you may become more enlightened, more severed, more spiritual, more aflame and that you may be humble and submissive, for as long as man does not consider himself to be good but regards himself as weak and deficient, he progresses; but the moment he considers himself good and says, "I am perfect", he falls into pride and retrogresses.

order.why: Consider the reported beginning of decline in a feeling of superiority.
shortened: There are some people who become proud and haughty and forget this fact. In their utter blindness they consider themselves to be somebody; then they fall from their high pedestal and great is the noise thereof.
Meekness and humility are the hallmarks of faith. As soon a believer feels himself the least bit superior to others, the beginning of his spiritual decline is commenced, all unaware to himself.

order.why: Keep the stringent reported counsel about superiority in its source’s voice.
Read vainglory as a garment that can be put aside.
Remember shared origin and mortality.
Hear the reported contrast between smallness and pride in origin.
shortened: This globe with all the infinite forms of life teeming through its length and breadth is but a grain of poppy in comparison to this stupendous creation and man is a part of this grain of poppy. Notwithstanding this infinitesimal smallness how proud, haughty is he of his origin!

order.why: Consider vanity as a demand for attention and approval.
shortened: Vanity is a form of egotism, an excessive desire for notice or approval of one's personal appearance or deeds. It is self-conceit and self-hypnotization.

order.why: Compare steady work with continual boasting.
Read the reported connection between excessive speech and the pursuit of reputation.
shortened: People speak too much because they seek fame, because they wish to be thought better than their brethren. Those who do most good say the least about it.

order.why: Consider the harm caused by seeking applause at another’s expense.
Keep the reported criticism of public self-display in its particular context.
Read the humorous reported portrait of a life organized around dress.
Consider the susceptibility created by a taste for flattery.
Read the reported fable of the crow and its lost cheese.
Compare pursuing fame with serving without seeking it.
Pause over the cost of name and fame.
Read the reported caution against imagining superior powers.
shortened: One must not think of becoming a leader. If anyone imagines himself the possessor of this or that high quality, and of certain superior powers not possessed by others, this will fill him with pride and haughtiness.

order.why: Keep the response to a request for leadership in its particular setting.
shortened: He wished to be made the leader of America and wrote plainly to me to this effect. One of the answers I gave him was, 'Cast aside all mention of the ruler and the ruled, the governor and the governed.'

order.why: Consider the reported loss associated with personal ambition.
Read the pursuit of office as an example of an organizing aim.
shortened: The objective point of another soul is to attain the highest official position. He strives day and night to gain the confidence of the public and the administrative authorities, so that they may promote him, through his merit, to the position of honour and fame among his fellow-men.

order.why: Keep the generalization about nobles attributed to its source.
shortened: O servant of the Supreme Lord! All nobles harbor desires for greatness and the melancholy of soaring ambition, that they might become exalted in the world or become leaders of others.

order.why: Hear the reported change in behavior after obtaining office.
shortened: The next day he was offered a government position with a good salary. Negligence overtoo[k] him and he became so proud that he would not even speak with me.

order.why: Read the danger of leadership becoming a form of name-worship.
Consider the reported way rivalry over precedence can displace shared purpose.
shortened: But afterwards this question of precedence will assume superlative importance in the estimation of men which will lead to quarrel and acrimonious thrusts. Why this change? Because those sweet Fragrances of the Days of the Manifestation are withheld; the hearts became cold and negligent; the eyes became blind; the ears deaf; pride, haughtiness, superciliousness and arrogance grip fast the souls of men; they lose their way to the radiant goal of heavenly Glory and every one exerts himself to attain to high position and honor.

order.why: Examine the effort to protect religious authority from discredit.
shortened: Consequently, such behavior can be attributed to naught save the petty-mindedness of such souls as tread the valley of arrogance and pride, are lost in the wilds of remoteness, walk in the ways of their idle fancy, and follow the dictates of the leaders of their faith.
With all their power and strength they strive to secure themselves in their petty pursuits, fearful lest the least discredit undermine their authority or blemish the display of their magnificence.

order.why: Read the particular account of deference, gifts, and fear of lost standing.
shortened: That is to say, through outward respect and the gift of a cloak and mantle, they manifest the utmost gratitude to any person, and should one be an absolute infidel, in their eyes he becometh like unto Joseph the truthful. One must deal with such persons accordingly. Their agitation and clamor arise from their fear lest their standing and respect be lost and they become abased and despised. Otherwise, were they to know that supreme respect and great consideration would be accorded them, they would outrun all others and show forth greater manifestations of certitude. The rabble are followers of every clamoring one, inclining with every wind....

order.why: Keep the rebuke of inflated educational claims within its specific address.
shortened: Yet with utmost pride they speak of political and social issues, violation of human dignity, and breach of divine laws. If only they had some knowledge of the political world and the relationships of social order! They are extremely egotistical and self-centered, yet completely unaware of human virtues and even of the sciences taught in schools. The height of their aspirations is to say "We studied in the advanced schools of Paris."

order.why: Read the reported distinction between a clerical position and actual understanding.
shortened: A clergy, assuming that he is ordained to his ministry he may think that he knows more about God, while the humble man in his congregation may know more. This sacerdotal and theological position makes many a clergy proud and haughty!

order.why: Consider learning and power in relation to their divine source.
Read knowledge’s purpose as guidance rather than pride against its source.
shortened: We have manifested knowledge that the servants might be guided unto My path, yet they have grown proud against the All-Informed One. Thus have We been treated by those who pride themselves on knowledge when He Who is known came with His name, the Self-Subsisting, and spoke that before which the Books of the Messengers have bowed down.

order.why: Keep the named example of learning without recognition in its historical setting.
shortened: Mulla 'Ali of Kand, who carried volumes of books and for years acquired sciences and arts which, in his own estimation, others were incapable and powerless to acquire, did not attain to the recognition of God, glorified be His majesty, and remained fixed and established in his own error.

order.why: Read the contrast between self-satisfaction and receptivity.
shortened: The self-satisfied learned ones were deprived of the bounties of God while you became privy to the mysteries of the Lord.

order.why: Consider humble seekers reaching what pride has obstructed.
shortened: This is among the signs of the grace of these days that souls who have spent a hundred years studying and discussing sciences and arts have been entirely deprived of divine bounties due to pride and arrogance, while blessed souls who are humble, suppliant and lowly have attained and been blessed - they have arrived at the shore of the Most Great Sea, reached the fountain of the water of life, tasted the sweetness of the love of God, have risen like guiding stars from the horizon of knowledge, and reposed in the shade of the Divine Lote Tree - so that the mystery of "your lowest are your highest" might become manifest and the sign of God's bounty might become known and celebrated.

order.why: Retain the warning about presumed accomplishment.
shortened: Those souls who considered themselves the most learned, distinguished and accomplished were not and are not mentioned in the presence of God.

order.why: Read the related contrast between self-estimation and divine recognition.
shortened: How many souls there are who have considered and still consider themselves the most exalted of creatures, unaware that they were and are not even mentioned in the presence of God.

order.why: Consider how small achievements can become barriers to mercy.
shortened: Through the composition of two words or the expression of vain imaginings, pride seizes him such that he becomes deprived of the ocean upon ocean of tenderness and mercy from the Truth, exalted be His glory.

order.why: Examine the possibility of worshipping a concept of inner reality one has fashioned.
Read the warning against turning spiritual language into a claim of independence.
shortened: And let not the ignorant among the people cling to these words and step into the arena of pride and vainglory, as hath been observed in some who, after being called for years to absolute wealth by the melodies of the Spirit, have finally claimed independence from the Truth. We seek refuge in God from this!

order.why: Warns against claiming a station reserved to the Manifestations.
Ask how religion, asceticism, or poverty itself can become an attachment.
Distinguish repeated prostration from an inward condition of humility.
shortened: O thou who prostrateth thyself at the threshold of the Ancient Beauty!

Prostration is evidence of the absence of being--that is, of utter humility, evanescence and nothingness. Yet today thou mayest observe peoples who, in their temples and cloisters of this nether world, would perform a thousand prostrations every minute, yet are steeped in pride, are haughty and stubborn. They have no knowledge whatsoever of submissiveness and lowliness before the threshold of the Self-Subsisting Lord, nor do they seek to worship the King of Divine Sovereignty.

order.why: Consider the spiritual traveler’s continuing vulnerability to pride.
shortened: Know, moreover, that should one who hath attained unto these stations and embarked upon these journeys fall prey to pride and vainglory, he would at that very moment come to naught and return to the first step without realizing it.

order.why: Read the reported test of an action through humility and self-projection.
shortened: The deed which is conducive to humility, meekness, submissiveness, evanescence, is accepted by God. The action which in the least connotes existence, pride, self-projection is human and not accepted by the Lord of mankind.

order.why: Hear the concise account of pride and submission.
shortened: He forbids pride and arrogance, which is the foundation of all vices, and commands submission and obedience, which is the foundation of virtues.

order.why: Retain the related statement of the roots of vice and virtue.
shortened: Observe how concise and beneficial it is - forbidding pride and haughtiness, which is the root of all vices, and calling to submission, which is the mother of all virtues.

order.why: Keep the reported emphasis on pride’s effect upon judgment.
shortened: Pride is the greatest sin - perhaps the only sin - leading to every other evil, warping the judgment.

order.why: Read the reported attraction of wealth and its capacity to occupy the self.
Distinguish the wine of recognition from the intoxication of vanity.
shortened: O ornament of the assured ones and delight of the eyes of the seekers! The world is in tumult and ferment, and humanity is intoxicated and bewildered. But their aims and conditions are different and diverse - one is inebriated from the overflowing divine cup, while another is drunk and proud from the wine of vanity. Some are dancing and rejoicing from the eternal wine of recognition, while others are unconscious and suffering from the deadly poison of heedlessness and error.

order.why: Keep the reported image of imagining oneself a sun in its admonitory setting.
shortened: There are some people who desire to wallow in the mud but they believe they are the world-illuminating Suns. I want to release them from this water and clay, clear their wings from these impediments but they cry out 'no, no we are suns and stars; we are not in need of thy education.'

order.why: Read the reported contrast between imagined powers and actual condition.
shortened: They are blind but suppose themselves to have been endowed with the all-searching eyes of the Omnipotence. They are deaf but imagine the all-hearing ears of the Almighty have been granted them. They are mute but they surmise the life-giving tongue of Christ is theirs. Bootless and vain are their imaginations!

order.why: Retain the example of self-bestowed spiritual titles.
Read the particular rebuke of untruthful statements that perplex others.
shortened: Certain statements proceeded from thee which were unworthy. Although at the time of thy presence thou wert counseled to speak naught but the truth and to become not the cause of people's perplexity, yet didst thou utter that which caused the people to be veiled, and at no time didst thou speak the truth.

order.why: Consider gratitude when success has been attributed wholly to one’s own effort.
shortened: Since in recent times some have become somewhat proud and have attributed this blessing and bounty to their own wisdom and efforts, therefore confusion has appeared so that they might awaken to realize that after their utter abasement, this honor and blessing was due to the grace and favor of the Blessed Beauty.

order.why: Read the related reported reminder of the source of spiritual gifts.
shortened: Those heedless and proud souls imagined that they had some merit and worthiness of their own, unaware that their relationship to the Cause of God was the source of that glory, and it was through the aid and protection of the Blessed Beauty that eyes were opened and ears became hearing.

order.why: Keep the brief reported failure to appreciate bounty.
shortened: However, some of them were heedless of the influences of the Most Exalted Pen - they did not know what was the cause of this honor. Rather, they fell into heedlessness and pride and did not appreciate the value of these bounties. Therefore they fell into tests and difficulties.

order.why: Hear the related image of absorption in selfish desires.
Read the account of an elevated person becoming proud before the source of elevation.
shortened: Beware lest anything prevent you from showing humility before God, and be not like unto him whose cause We exalted among the servants and whose mention We spread throughout the lands. Yet when he saw himself in glory and elevation, he waxed proud before Him Who created and fashioned him, reaching such a state that he opposed the Countenance and was neglectful of God's rights, and was of those who, when the Sun of Beauty shone forth from the horizon of grandeur, grew arrogant and were of those who are proud.

order.why: Keep the particular letter and its quoted warning together.
shortened: O thou who hast with all thy being arisen to serve the Covenant! The letter received from that known individual is steeped in pride and vanity.

And in the Tablet of the Temple He explicitly states: "We chose one of our brothers and elevated him to a station where pride and arrogance seized him, therefore We returned him" to the end of the verse.

order.why: Consider rank becoming an occasion for hostility.
Read the reported danger of treating closeness to Baha’u’llah as personal superiority.
Keep the reported incident and its language of punishment within its historical setting.
Read the recollected claim of exceptional service as a reported incident.
Consider the related reported confusion of bestowed opportunity with personal entitlement.
shortened: In any case, at the time when Mirza Aqa Jan should have attained the good-pleasure of the Blessed One, at the critical moment, he lost himself because he imagined that this elevated station was of his own doing. In the latter days he had carried his audacity to such a degree that, in the presence of the Blessed Beauty, he had said: "Had His Holiness the Exalted One been in my place, He would not have endured it."

order.why: Retain the reported comparison of particular figures without generalizing its accusations.
shortened: A question was asked regarding the elder brother and the Master replied: In any cycle or time someone has shown pride. In the time of Christ it was Judas. In the days of the Blessed Perfection, Subhi Ezel. Now it is the head of the Nakazeen.

order.why: Keep the reported remark about Muhammad-Ali in its attribution.
shortened: Sheikh As'ad had said that this Mirza Muhammad Ali is so weighty with his pride that when he sits down, he does not rise again...

order.why: Read ancestral pride through its particular historical example.
shortened: But they did not listen. Rather, they were intoxicated with the wine of pride, saying "We are of the lineage of the Kayanis! We are the descendants of Rustam the mighty!"

order.why: Consider the account of seeking an illustrious lineage.
shortened: When Mirza Aqa Khan was Prime Minister and held Iran under his control, he wished to trace his lineage to a famous person. One of the inhabitants of the village of Bukh traced his ancestry to Khwajih Abu-Salt-i-Harvi, who had a maidservant, and this family of Khwajih are descended from that Khwajih. The Prime Minister and his people all celebrated that "Praise be to God, we are descended from Khwajih Abu-Salt," and Khwajih Abu-Salt was someone who served Imam Rida, peace be upon him.

order.why: Hear the reported question about what people choose to boast of.
Read the examples of Nimrod and Pharaoh through the theme of passing power.
Retain the related comparison within its source’s rebuke.
shortened: Each became a mighty Pharaoh and a severely arrogant Nimrod. They were wholly deprived of the favors of the Day of Resurrection and were rendered hopeless of the gifts of the All-Forgiving Lord.

order.why: Keep the reported contrast between protecting the oppressed and magnifying oneself.
shortened: Some of the kings exhibited pride, one was the Ottoman king, Abdul Aziz Khan.
You proclaimed once that you were a defender of the oppressed, but it becomes evident that you are not; rather, you magnify your own selfish desires and passions.

order.why: Read the particular advice about approaching an emperor in its historical setting.
Consider pride within the passage’s account of opposition to revelation.
Hear the appeal to humility before the divine Manifestation.
shortened: O My creation! Be not proud before Him at Whose face the countenances of the Concourse on High bow down in adoration, and be not of the arrogant ones.

order.why: Read the devotional image of creation bowing before God.
shortened: At this moment all who are in the heavens and on earth prostrated themselves before God, and the Holy Spirit breathed into the temples of the Concourse on High, and the Dove warbled in the midmost heart of eternity, and all necks bowed down before His command, while the proud were in the fire of hell and grievous peril, and verily He was witness over all things.

order.why: Close the linked readings with prayer for the guidance of proud souls.
shortened: We beseech Him to guide such souls as have drunk the wine of pride and are heedless of that which profiteth them.

order.why: Read the supplied sayings from Proverbs with their citations intact.
Distinguish respect for achievement from self-aggrandizement.
End with intellectual honesty and humility before what is not yet understood.

questions: How might the appearance of humility conceal a desire for recognition or rank?
What distinguishes acknowledging an ability or achievement from feeling superior to another person?
How can honest self-examination coexist with confidence in human nobility and capacity to grow?
What do the two prayers in Luke 18:9–14 reveal about comparing one’s righteousness with someone else’s?
How might a community honor service and achievement without feeding rivalry or dependence on applause?
What practices help learning remain open to correction and to mysteries beyond one’s present understanding?

references.label: 1 · Luke 18:9–14 · Two prayers and the danger of self-righteousness
references.note: The King James Version introduces the parable as directed toward people confident in their own righteousness who despise others. Compare its contrasting prayers with the compilation’s concern about outward humility, self-examination, and forgiveness. Read the figures as a challenge to the reader’s own motives, not as grounds for stereotyping a religious community.

subjects.displayTitle: Material progress: what makes advancement humane?
subjects.introduction: Asked about a canal, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá answered that the work was most acceptable and beloved, because the friends of the Merciful must labour for the prosperity of the world until they become mercy made visible. The fleeting nature of this life, He insists, is no excuse for leaving it unimproved; the Qur’án itself prays for good in this world as well as the next. So Bahá’u’lláh commands beneficial sciences, commerce, industry and agriculture, and ‘Abdu’l-Bahá ties them to character and justice: when morals improve, the arts flourish, and through justice trade thrives and education spreads. Yet He had watched the same century that produced the telegraph and the aeroplane arm itself with cannon and torpedo, and He warns that outward powers have raced ahead of the inner ones. Education, He says, can turn a bitter mountain fruit sweet and make a cowardly nation brave; and the moment any society stops ascending, decline begins. The house built by wisdom and established by understanding in Proverbs offers a compact image of prosperity that rests on something deeper than production [1]. From here the way opens onto the harmony of science and religion, the dignity of agriculture, the call to serve humanity, and the distinction between the two kinds of civilization, material and spiritual, that together make advancement humane.
subjects.arc: Move from useful work and its moral purpose through the possibilities and dangers of invention, then examine education, collective action, and continuing spiritual growth.

order.why: Connect flourishing industry with truthfulness and character.
shortened: When characters are improved, sciences and arts flourish; minds become vastly enlightened; hearts are filled with truthfulness and trustworthiness, with zeal, devotion, and determination; statesmanship attaineth its highest degree; new industries become widespread; commerce is expanded; and courage and audacity raise aloft their banner. The nation passeth from one condition to another. It becometh a new creation, and the verse "Blessed, therefore, be God, the most excellent of Makers!" is realized.

order.why: Open with a canal as a concrete expression of mercy.
Establish why a fleeting world still deserves improvement.
Read justice as a condition of commerce, education, and international friendship.
Confront invention’s destructive use in warfare.
Consider aviation’s competing possibilities of service and destruction.
Examine the delay of inward virtues amid outward efficiency.
shortened: If we review history, we will observe that human advancement has been greatest in the development of material virtues. Civilization is the sign and evidence of this progression. Throughout the world, material civilization has attained truly wonderful heights and degrees of efficiency -- that is to say, the outward powers and virtues of man have greatly developed, but the inner and ideal virtues have been correspondingly delayed and neglected.

order.why: Retain the related concern about neglected spiritual civilization.
Join material and spiritual advancement.
shortened: Therefore, O friends of the Ancient Beauty and O fellow-citizens of the Greatest Name, strive that you may make tremendous progress in all ranks, both spiritual and material.

order.why: Read beneficial sciences and agriculture within a religious account of civilization.
Turn to practical work, invention, commerce, and avoidance of corruption.
Consider public education and useful sciences as public responsibilities.
Read the reported emphasis on results that alleviate suffering.
Trace the effects attributed to education.
shortened: Now observe that it is education that brings East and West under man's dominion, produces all these marvellous crafts, promotes these mighty arts and sciences, and gives rise to these new discoveries and undertakings.

order.why: Consider education’s influence upon character as well as skill.
shortened: Through education the ignorant become learned, the cowardly become courageous, the crooked branch becomes straight, the acrid and bitter fruit of the mountains and woods becomes sweet and succulent, and the five-petalled flower puts forth a hundred petals. Through education barbarous nations become civilized and even animals take on human-like manners. Education must be accorded the greatest importance; for just as diseases are highly communicable in the world of bodies, so is character highly communicable in the realm of hearts and spirits.

order.why: Read continuing improvement in the education of children.
Keep the reported account of officials and schooling in its historical setting.
Consider communication making worldwide association possible.
shortened: In this day, however, means of communication have multiplied, and the five continents of the earth have virtually merged into one. And for everyone it is now easy to travel to any land, to associate and exchange views with its peoples, and to become familiar, through publications, with the conditions, the religious beliefs and the thoughts of all men.

order.why: Read the interpretation of the earth being brought near to itself.
shortened: O servant of Baha! It is related in the traditions that, on the Day of Resurrection, the earth shall be brought near unto itself. Yet they knew not that wondrous industries would make East and West companions, and new discoveries would cause North and South to share each other’s secrets.

order.why: Retain the reported experience of shrinking travel times.
Read railways and steam within the source’s religious appreciation.
shortened: Truly, if not for railroads and the power of steam, how could these long distances be traversed with such ease? This is one of the miracles of this promised century of our current age.

order.why: Consider changed circumstances as a setting for religious teaching.
shortened: The progress of the world during the past fifteen hundred years has greatly modified the conditions which prevailed when these teachers were on earth. Man has learned to control the forces of nature and to harness them in his service. All the nations of the world are in constant, easy, and rapid communication: closely united by the telegraph, the telephone, steam and electric locomotion.

order.why: Connect inventions with cooperation and emerging international laws.
Read the reported example of American union and advancement.
shortened: When the American nation united, how much it led to their happiness, progress and civilization. If this unity and agreement did not exist among the United States, this progress in sciences, arts and advancement would not have been achieved.

order.why: Hear the reported contrast with earlier conditions of unity and peace.
Retain the source’s expectation concerning peace and a hidden science.
Keep the interview’s speaker attribution and warning about commercial competition.
Read the reported concern about crowded cities as a historical observation.
Consider inventions that earlier observers could not imagine.
Read humanity’s relation to nature through the passage’s rhetorical imagery.
shortened: However man has seized the sword from nature and with it is beating nature back. For example, the natural law is for man to remain on earth. Yet, he swims in the sea like a fish or flies in the air like a bird. Or the law of nature is for electricity to flow freely. But we see that man has captured this power in the confines of a bulb. The nature of man is to see for a proscribed distance and to hear only over a limited space. However, man has devised means to observe the heavens above and to communicate with every corner of the globe.

order.why: Trace widening knowledge and artistic capacities.
shortened: Man is always progressing. His circle of knowledge is ever widening, and his mental activity flows through many and varied channels. Look what man has accomplished in the field of science, consider his many discoveries and countless inventions and his profound understanding of natural law.
In the world of art it is just the same, and this wonderful development of man's faculties becomes more and more rapid as time goes on.

order.why: Survey the new scope of sciences, arts, and inventions.
shortened: See how, in this day, the scope of sciences and arts hath widened out, and what wondrous technical advances have been made, and to what a high degree the mind's powers have increased, and what stupendous inventions have appeared.

order.why: Read the source’s account of uncovering hidden natural realities.
shortened: In this radiant age, humanity has made extraordinary progress in every respect. In the world of science, manifold advancements have been achieved, how many hidden realities of creation have been discovered, and the holy power of the mind has unveiled the concealed mysteries and protected truths of the natural world, has broken through the laws of nature, and brought those hidden mysteries from the realm of the unseen into the visible realm.
How much has the world of industry advanced, how much has the scope of inventions expanded!

order.why: Consider communication technologies as images of transformation.
Hear the image of arts and crafts surging like a sea.
Read the growth of sciences over a long historical span.
Keep the reported comparison of modern rooms with royal luxuries.
shortened: For example, let us take this room. Cyrus the great King of Persia could not enjoy the luxuries of a room like this. Solomon with all his glories had a mirror like this! (and he took me jokingly before the large mirror and said: look in it!) Solomon had not an automobile but only a wooden carriage, a little gilded. The audience chamber of Alexander the great was not lighted with electricity. Now most everybody enjoys the possession of an automobile or his room is lighted with electricity.

order.why: Consider the reported account of comfort and transformed everyday life.
Retain the aviation forecast as a reported historical expectation.
shortened: The science of aviation will make great progress in the immediate future and people will travel at ease from one city to another city without any danger. It will become as popular as automobiles.
Just as now every well to do person has an automobile, then they will have an aeroplane.

order.why: Keep the reported celebration of discoverers and its period’s rhetoric attributed.
Move from new material conditions to the broader need for renewal.
Notice renewal extending into ordinary habits and institutions.
Consider new capacities and moralities for changing human needs.
shortened: Humanity has emerged from its former degrees of limitation and preliminary training. Man must now become imbued with new virtues and powers, new moralities, new capacities. New bounties, bestowals and perfections are awaiting and already descending upon him. The gifts and graces of the period of youth, although timely and sufficient during the adolescence of the world of mankind, are now incapable of meeting the requirements of its maturity.

order.why: Retain the related reported description of renewed thought and invention.
Hear the reported sequence of reformation and regeneration.
Read the reported succession of organizing ideas in different ages.
Consider the argument for religious renewal in national advancement.
Read spiritual renewal through its claimed historical effects.
Consider gradual development through the image of a growing child.
shortened: A nursing infant must be nurtured for years in the father's arms before reaching maturity and adulthood. Now is but the beginning of that luminous morning; gradually, rays like the dawn's light are becoming visible and perceptible.

order.why: Read the reported image of maturity and a century reflecting earlier ages.
Retain the related reported contrast with previous centuries.
Keep the historical comparison of Europe and America in its period’s vocabulary.
shortened: Today throughout the five continents of the globe it is Europe and most sections of America that are renowned for law and order, government and commerce, art and industry, science, philosophy and education. Yet in ancient times these were the most savage of the world's peoples, the most ignorant and brutish. They were even stigmatized as barbarians -- that is, utterly rude and uncivilized.

The basis of Europe's progress and civilization was actually laid in the fifteenth century of the Christian era, and from that time on, all her present evident culture has been, under the stimulus of great minds and as a result of the expansion of the frontiers of knowledge and the exertion of energetic and ambitious efforts, in the process of development.

order.why: Read the appeal for progress and international assistance in its particular setting.
shortened: Observe how other countries have advanced in modern progress. The Ancient Beauty has guided you through all counsels and covenants to that which causes life and progress in stations. You must be the party of progress so that you may become the army of life and the hosts of salvation. Likewise, divine confirmations have prepared for you the means of progress from every direction. Soon your brothers from Europe and America will come to Iran and will establish novel industries, build works of civilization, various factories, promote commerce, multiply agriculture, and spread knowledge.

order.why: Consider the reported appraisal of Paris as a historical judgment.
shortened: Indeed, Paris has achieved the utmost progress in civilization and has attained success and prosperity in all material affairs, reaching such a state that it is like a mirror reflecting infinite images of civilization.

order.why: Read the tree’s growth and anticipated fruit in the reported appraisal of America.
Retain the reported distinction between material achievement and higher ideals.
Keep the broad reported comparison of political attitudes in its historical setting.
Read the reported comparison of Western and Islamic societies without making it a present forecast.
Consider the reported call for changed habits and generous impulses.
Retain the particular address concerning the Parsees.
shortened: The glance of divine favor in this Most Great Cycle has encompassed all the Parsees, and thus they have made various kinds of progress in all ranks and conditions.

order.why: Read the anticipation of women’s advancing capacities.
shortened: Day by day they are advancing. Soon you will observe that among women, souls will arise so attracted that they will cause amazement. They will become brilliant lamps and speakers of the proofs and evidences of the Lord of Bounties.

order.why: Keep the call to service and growing awareness within its particular address.
shortened: This bounty will be manifested when all subjects comprehend the benevolent intentions of the just Shepherd and do not fall short in rendering outstanding services as enjoined by the decisive texts, and increase their awareness day by day until the lights of civilization, like the rays of dawn, illumine the horizons of the country.

order.why: Read the related account of public service and development.
Treat the sweeping comparison of centuries as the source’s rhetorical appraisal.
Retain the related comparison and its original omission.
shortened: For example, if you compare the effects, discoveries, knowledge, arts, wonders, sciences and learning of fifty centuries with this luminous century, surely the virtues of this divine century exceed the achievements of all past centuries.

Likewise the arts, wonders, technical discoveries, beneficial projects, complete civilization, expansion of thoughts, increase of understanding and comprehension, revelation of the mysteries of creation and manifestation of the realities of contingent beings - this matter is universally accepted and all acknowledge and confess it.

order.why: Hear the source’s celebration of a distinctive age.
shortened: O friends of God! This cycle and dispensation cannot be compared to former ages, for previous eras were but a ray of this era, and former centuries but a token of this century. Observe ye the progress and exaltation of this mighty century, which is distinguished in all aspects and conditions. It is the sun of all ages and centuries - its traces brilliant, its lights manifest, its power overwhelming, and its radiance adorning both East and West. Its crafts bewilder minds, its wonders gladden souls, its sciences illuminate the world, its arts are the very life of the world and eternal life.

order.why: Read the reported description of light and discovery in its religious setting.
Retain the reported sequence linking love, science, and civilization.
shortened: This age is the age of light. This century is the radiant century. This cycle is the cycle of love. This period is the period of sciences. This epoch is the epoch of universal civilization.

order.why: Keep the reported interpretation of spiritual and material greatness together.
shortened: Aside from the true meaning of this passage which pertains to the power and might of the Cause of God, to the revelation of verses and signs, to the solution of divine problems, to the disclosure of the mysteries of the Holy Book and to the spread of knowledge - each of which is a hundred times greater in this mighty revelation than in any previous one - materially, too, all the learned men of this age agree that the advancements in knowledge, the arts, industries and inventions of this century are equal to those of the last fifty centuries, indeed, even greater than that.

order.why: Read the numerical comparison as the passage’s sweeping claim, not a measured statistic.
shortened: Thus you observe that the effects, results, sciences, arts, wonders, crafts, discoveries and undertakings in this one blessed age are many times greater than all previous centuries combined. That is, if you were to gather the achievements of a hundred centuries, they would not equal one-tenth of the achievements of this century.

order.why: Hear the praise of discovery and an expanding sphere of thought.
shortened: Praise be to God that the radiant century hath come. Praise be to God the springtime of Eternity hath pitched its tent. Praise be to God, this is the age of the discovery of the realities of things.
Verily I say unto you, this age is the age of science. This age is the age of the appearance of the truth. This age is the age of the extension of the sphere of thought.

order.why: Retain the reported celebration of enlightenment in its original terms.
Read the reported summary connecting progress with peace and unity.
shortened: These are the fundamental principles of progress, civilization, international peace and the unity of mankind. These are the essentials of Baha'u'llah's teachings, the secret of everlasting health, the remedy and healing for man.

order.why: Consider mature work by the results it yields.
Read progress among the fruits of human and spiritual virtues.
shortened: And the fruit, effect, leaves, flowers and blossoms of these trees are the human perfections, virtues and characteristics, spiritual sanctification and detachment both inward and outward, divine qualities, and modern progress.

order.why: Weighs the advances of material civilization against its destructive capacities.
Consider the reported relation of renewed vigor to moral reconstruction.
shortened: When man thus adorns himself, he will progress every day with new vigor; his soul will become more and more sensitized and the laws and morals of the world will be reconstructed with divine conviction.

order.why: Read continual spiritual and material advancement as an ongoing responsibility.
shortened: The glory and joy and spirit and fragrance of the human world lies in this: that it should continuously and successively advance toward spiritual progress, and thereafter make material progress. If thought is not directed toward constant progress, it is stagnation.
Likewise in physical matters and sciences and arts, man must be constantly progressing and increasing in knowledge. The moment there is a halt, decline occurs.
Man must ever be ascending.

order.why: Retain the related reported warning about stagnation.
shortened: Abdul Baha: "Stagnation is the cause of retrogression. Man must always advance. As soon as man remains stationary in a certain cause he will go backward. Therefore he must strive that man may advance day by day, that he may progress in all the worlds.

order.why: Compare the separately reported account of standstill and progress without flattening its difference.
Keep the brief account of progress in a world of opposites.
shortened: Know thou that progress is of two kinds: one is progress in station and the other is progress in perfections. Progress in station pertains to this world, as thou observest that the human body was first in the mineral state, then from the mineral state it advanced to the vegetable state, and from the vegetable to the animal state, and from the animal to the human state, thus progressing through stations. This progress in station belongs to this world of opposites.

order.why: Read the reported image of civilization moving among different regions.
Consider growth and movement within the source’s account of the universe.
shortened: There is motion in all created things and movement and growth in all existing atoms. The universe is progressing and cycles are in utmost adornment and receptivity. Humankind has an abundant portion and will have an unlimited share.

order.why: Hear the affirmation of endless progress.
Keep the reported comparison of spiritual acceleration in its own terms.
shortened: Among these matters is progress, among these matters is drawing near unto God - meaning the progress that would depend on fifty thousand years is achieved in one day for souls.

order.why: Read the reported priority of spiritual power.
Close with the reported vision joining discovery, refinement, and moral illumination.

questions: What makes a practical improvement, such as a canal or a new means of travel, an expression of care for humanity?
How might a community judge whether its technical capacities and its moral capacities are developing together?
What responsibilities follow when the same invention can relieve suffering or intensify destruction?
How does the house built by wisdom in Proverbs 24:3–4 illuminate the relation between knowledge, character, and lasting prosperity?
How should readers approach the historical comparisons and reported expectations here while forming their own judgments about progress?
What connections among education, agriculture, justice, and service could guide a local effort to improve collective life?

references.label: 1 · Proverbs 24:3–4 · Building through wisdom and understanding
references.note: The King James Version connects a house’s construction, establishment, and enrichment with wisdom, understanding, and knowledge. Compare that image with the compilation’s links between character and material prosperity. This is a wisdom image for reflection, not a technical program for economic development.

subjects.displayTitle: The Primal Word: meaning before syllable or sound
subjects.introduction: Bahá’u’lláh describes a Word uttered without syllable or sound, exalted above every substance the senses can perceive, and yet the cause by which all that exists stepped out of nothingness. The Essence of God stays barred to every seeker; what can be known is the Will that God created through itself, the first point mentioned in contingent being, which the Báb calls a single Will shining forth in each age under a new name. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá makes the idea tangible: created things are like separate letters, which carry no complete meaning, while Christ is like an entire word, because a whole meaning can be read from Him, the spotless mirror in which the sun’s light and heat appear. John’s prologue, with its Word that was with God and became flesh, is the text He is interpreting, and the two accounts can be set side by side without being flattened into one [1]. Then the Word turns practical: it educates, quickens, and draws estranged people into fellowship. The way forward runs through the Primal Will, the Holy Spirit, and the Manifestation of God as mediator between the hidden Essence and ourselves.
subjects.arc: Begin with the soundless Word, explore manifestation and divine transcendence, then follow the images of point and letters into revelation, remembrance, and lived transformation.

order.why: Open with a Word beyond syllable, sound, and substance.
Explore Christ as the complete meaning reflected in a spotless mirror.
shortened: For by the Word is not meant the body of Christ but the divine perfections that were manifested in Him. Thus Christ was like a spotless mirror which was turned towards the Sun of Truth, and the perfections of that Sun, that is, its light and heat, were plainly manifest in that mirror. If we look into the mirror, we see the sun and we say it is the sun.

The perfections of Christ are called the Word since all created things are like individual letters, and individual letters do not convey a complete meaning; while the perfections of Christ are even as an entire word, for from a word a complete meaning can be inferred.

order.why: Distinguish the eternal station of manifestation from contingent beginnings.
shortened: The third station is that of divine manifestation and heavenly splendour, which is the Word of God, the everlasting Grace, and the Holy Spirit. This station has neither beginning nor end; for firstness and lastness pertain to the contingent world and not to the world of God.

order.why: Read the distinction between the unknowable Essence and knowledge through the Manifestations.
shortened: Assuming the truth of this hypothesis, "attainment unto the divine Presence" is in this sense obviously possible to no one, inasmuch as this revelation is confined to the innermost Essence, unto which no man can attain. "The way is barred, and all seeking rejected." The minds of the favorites of heaven, however high they soar, can never attain this station, how much less the understanding of obscured and limited minds.

The knowledge of Him, Who is the Origin of all things, and attainment unto Him, are impossible save through knowledge of, and attainment unto, these luminous Beings who proceed from the Sun of Truth. By attaining, therefore, to the presence of these holy Luminaries, the "Presence of God" Himself is attained.

order.why: Consider the Primal Will as a universal reality.
shortened: The world of Command is the station of the Primal Will which is a universal reality that is resolved into infinite forms.

order.why: Relates the Primal Will to successive appearances of the Sun of Reality.
Read creation through Will while preserving the distinction from the divine Essence.
Consider speech as manifestation without encompassing the Speaker.
shortened: Know that His word encompasses all things and flows through all worlds, for speech is a manifestation among the manifestations of the Speaker. God, exalted be He, made it the manifestation of His encompassing nature and His revelation, and of all His appearances, for the Essence alone encompasses itself, and He is the Encompasser and nothing encompasses Him.

order.why: Examine the Bayan’s distinctions among divine Essence, creative utterance, and recurrent manifestation.
shortened: And that is none other than the utterance of the Will, which is the utterance of God: for the Eternal Essence hath ever been, and ever shall be, in a single state, while utterance belongeth to the realm of creation and innovation; and since in the Will naught is seen but God alone, this utterance is accordingly attributed unto God: for none but God is able to produce its like.

Rather, from the beginning that hath no beginning till the end that hath no end, there hath always been, and will continue forever to be, one single Will, Who shineth forth in each Dispensation by a specific Revelation, becoming the Manifestation of "He shall not be asked of His doing, and He doeth what he willeth."

order.why: Distinguish investigative human perception from the universal divine Intellect.
shortened: The spiritual power associated with the world of nature is the power of investigation, and it is through investigation that it discovers the realities and properties of things. But the heavenly intellectual power, which is beyond nature, encompasses, knows and comprehends all things, is aware of the divine mysteries, truths and inner meanings, and discovers the hidden verities of the Kingdom. This divine intellectual power is confined to the holy Manifestations and the Daysprings of prophethood. A ray of this light falls upon the mirrors of the hearts of the righteous, that they may also receive, through the holy Manifestations, a share and benefit of this power.

order.why: Read the wayfarer’s encounter with the Intellect and the accompanying poetic image.
shortened: 15 If the wayfarers be among them that dwell in the court of the All-Praised, this is the station of the Intellect, which is known as the messenger of the realm of the body and the most great pillar. That which is intended, however, is the universal divine Intellect, whose sovereignty fostereth the growth of all things, and not every vain and feeble mind. Thus hath the wise Sana'i written:
"How can feeble reason embrace the Qur'an
Or the spider snare a phoenix in its web?

order.why: Consider the limits of finite understanding before the promised mysteries.
shortened: 68 God, the Most High, hath placed these signs in men so that veiled minds might not deny the mysteries of the life beyond, nor belittle that which hath been promised them. For some hold fast to reason and deny whatever reason comprehendeth not, and yet feeble minds can never grasp the reality of the stages that we have related: The universal divine Intellect alone can comprehend them.

order.why: Return to the relation of letters, complete meaning, and the reality of Christ.
Retain the related reported explanation of divine virtues and the Word.
Read the reported identification of the Word with divine knowledge.
Keep the short reported response in its original attribution.
shortened: Abdul Baha: They have asked if it is possible for a person to reach the station of Christ, - whoever suffers of prays, can he reach this station?
No! It cannot be, because Christ was the Word of God, the Holy Spirit.

order.why: Consider the Word in the account of humanity’s spiritual nature.
shortened: Question:  In 1 Corinthians 15:22 it is written:  "For as in Adam all die, even so in Christ shall all be made alive."  What is the meaning of these words?

Answer:  Know that there are two natures in man:  the material and the spiritual.  The material nature is inherited from Adam, while the spiritual nature is inherited from the reality of the Word of God, which is the spirituality of Christ.  The material nature is born of Adam, but the spiritual nature is born of the grace of the Holy Spirit.  The material nature is the source of every imperfection and the spiritual nature is the source of all perfection.

order.why: Read the apostles as letters receiving the Word’s reflected splendor.
Connect the Word with education and quickening life.
shortened: The Sun of Truth is the Word of God, upon which dependeth the education of those who are endowed with the power of understanding and of utterance. It is the true spirit and the heavenly water, through whose aid and gracious providence all things have been and will be quickened.

order.why: Read its transformative purpose in turning hostility toward fellowship.
shortened: And this is clear: a power above and beyond the powers of nature must needs be brought to bear, to change this black darkness into light, and these hatreds and resentments, grudges and spites, these endless wrangles and wars, into fellowship and love amongst all the peoples of the earth. This power is none other than the breathings of the Holy Spirit and the mighty inflow of the Word of God.

order.why: Hear the reported image of love gathering people for shared nourishment.
shortened: The Word of God is Love. It has gathered us together to partake of material and spiritual food....

order.why: Consider the prayer’s account of creation being transformed by the First Word.
shortened: I testify that no sooner had the First Word proceeded, through the potency of Thy will and purpose, out of His mouth, and the First Call gone forth from His lips than the whole creation was revolutionized, and all that are in the heavens and all that are on earth were stirred to the depths. Through that Word the realities of all created things were shaken, were divided, separated, scattered, combined and reunited, disclosing, in both the contingent world and the heavenly kingdom, entities of a new creation, and revealing, in the unseen realms, the signs and tokens of Thy unity and oneness.

order.why: Read the Word in relation to created realities and the sending of Messengers.
Retain the concise affirmation of the Originator bringing forth His Word.
Consider the Word in human form as a center of attraction.
Hear the Will speaking in human form and the problem of hearing it.
Read the Word’s appearance at the appointed time.
shortened: And when the appointed time was fulfilled and the Hour had struck, the Word shone forth above the horizon of the Will of God.

order.why: Consider the varying stations and names applied to the Word.
Enter the symbolism of point, letters, light, and the Most Great Remembrance.
shortened: This Point is the focal centre of the circle of Names and marketh the culmination of the manifestations of Letters in the world of creation. Through it have appeared indications of the impenetrable Mystery, the adorned Symbol, He Who standeth revealed in the Most Great Name -- a Name which is recorded in the luminous Tablet and is inscribed in the holy, the blessed, the snow-white Scroll. And when the Point was joined to the second Letter which appeareth in the beginning of the Mathani, it traversed the heavens of exposition and utterance. Then the eternal Light of God shed its radiance, flared up in the midmost heart of the firmament of testimony and produced two Luminaries.

order.why: Read the Primal Point through the associated images of Word, Book, and Balance.
Keep the extensive reported interpretation of letters and numbers distinct from the revealed selections.
shortened: In the dogmatic teachings about the Qur'an, called Hadith, it says: "Everything that is in the Qur'an lies in the first Surih, the Fatihah, and everything that is in the Fatihah is to be found in the first sentence: Bismi'llahi'r-Rahmani'r-Rahim = in the Name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate, and everything in this first sentence is contained in the "bi" (its initial letter), and everything contained in the "bi" is to be found in the point under the "bi" (its smallest part), and I (the Prophet, here 'Ali) (successor and interpreter of Muhammad and the Qur'an) am the Point (Nuqtih) under the "bi"." - His Holiness the Bab has found from counting the letters of the phrase: Bismi'llahi'r-Rahmani'r-Rahim that the number 19 represents the mystic basic number of the cosmos (universe). This mystic basic number 19 at the same time represents the Logos, the Manifestation, the Emanation of God, which can at the same time be designated by the "bi" or the point (nuqtih) under the "bi".

order.why: Read the symbolic account of Adam, Eve, Will, and Desire in its own setting.
Consider the Point’s response to divine love and the covenant described here.
shortened: God hath not created anything except that He hath taken from it a covenant of His Lordship. This is a Day whereon God hath offered His love unto all things, and the first to respond was the Point of the Bayan. Therefore hath He made him the Manifestation of His Self in that Ridvan and bestowed upon him that which none in Paradise hath been given, from the beginning that hath no beginning unto the end that hath no end.

order.why: Read the Qayyumu’l-Asma’s many addresses concerning the Remembrance together.
shortened: O King of the Muslims! After the Book, aid Our Most Great Remembrance in truth, for verily God hath ordained for thee and for those who circle round thee, on the Day of Resurrection, a station of questioning upon the Bridge, according to the truth.

By God! If ye do good, ye do it for your own selves, and if ye deny God and His signs, verily We through God can dispense with all creation and dominion, in truth. O people of the earth! Whoso obeyeth God's Remembrance and this His Book hath indeed obeyed God and His friends in truth, and shall be recorded in the hereafter as one of the people of the Garden of Good-Pleasure with God.

O concourse of divines! Fear God in your opinions from this your day, for the Remembrance among you from Us is in truth a judge and witness. Turn away from that which ye take from other than God's Book of truth, for ye shall in truth be questioned at your station on the path on the Day of Resurrection.
O people! If ye believe in God alone, then follow Me in this Most Great Remembrance from your Lord, that God may forgive you your sins.

And in the origination of the signs and the hours and the souls and the horizons are signs for those of understanding among you who are witness to the remembrance of God, the Most High. Fear God and speak not concerning the Most Great Remembrance of God anything besides God, for verily We have taken His covenant from every Prophet and His people regarding His remembrance, and We send not the Messengers save with this firm covenant.

We have, of a truth, perfected Our favor upon the dwellers of the heavens and earth through the bounty of the Remembrance, in truth, as a blessing. God hath made the supreme blessing in this your Day to be the remembrance of God, the Most High, and God is witness over all things.

Verily God created Joseph and his brethren in the realms of holiness from a sprinkling upon a name from the drop of creation, from that water brought into being. When We found in Joseph love for the Most Great Remembrance, We clothed him, by God's leave, in the garments of prophethood, according to what was decreed for him in the Mother Book around the Fire.

He is the Remembrance from God to give you glad tidings of His promise and to warn you of His vengeance, and He is the One concealed in the Mother Book, preserved at the Point of Fire according to what was in the mystery of the Book.
He is the Remembrance before you, to your right, and to your left, by God's leave in truth, that people might be mentioned in truth around the Gate through the wondrous verses in this Book.
O people of the earth! Deal not with the Most Great Remembrance as the community dealt with Husayn unjustly in the Holy Land.

Know, O servants of God, the Light hath come to you from God, the Exalted, in truth mighty and resplendent, that ye may seek of His grace what God hath ordained in His dominion, in truth by truth, as a decree.
And verily man, in truth, with God your True Master, is he who gathereth around the water. And verily the beast, in truth, is he who is cast forth from around the Fire.

O people of the earth! Hold fast to the cord of God, the Impregnable -- Our Remembrance, this Arabian Youth Who hath been concealed at the point of ice upon seas of fire. Remember in His presence, after His permission, God's favors upon you, and conceal not the truth in His presence. Know ye not that God knoweth whatsoever is in the heavens and earth, what ye conceal and what ye reveal?

God encompasseth all things. Whoso is an enemy to God and His angels and His messengers after the Remembrance hath come unto them from God -- We are witnesses of their unbelief, and in the life to come they shall have no portion save a mighty fire.

Fear God, O company of kings, regarding distance from the Remembrance after the Truth has come to you with the Book and verses from God through the tongue of the Remembrance wondrously. Seek bounty from God, for after your belief, God has ordained for you a garden whose breadth is as the breadth of all gardens, wherein you shall find naught but blessings and bounties from God, according to that which was great in the Mother Book.

God, besides Whom there is none other true God, saith: Indeed, whoso visiteth the Remembrance of God after His passing, it is as though he hath attained the presence of the Lord, seated upon His mighty Throne.

He is an Arab youth who has been concealed around the fire in the Mother Book. God has revealed to Me in truth within the House of Kaaba: "Verily, I am God, there is no God but I. I have chosen you for Myself and selected the Remembrance for yourself.
Verily this Remembrance is the remnant of the lights, and He is better for you if ye be faithful to God, the Most High, in truth and by truth.

We have sent no Prophet but We took from him a covenant concerning the Remembrance and His Day. Verily the Remembrance of God and His Day have been witnessed in truth at the Most Exalted Prospect before the angels of the Throne.

order.why: Consider the Primal Point in new attire and the interpretation of the Bayan.
shortened: Verily this is the Primal Point, arrayed in His new attire and manifested in His glorious Name. He at present beholdeth everything from this Horizon. Indeed He is supreme over all things.

Say, O people, fulfil whatever ye understand of the Persian Bayan and whatever ye understand not ask this unerring Remembrance that He may set forth clearly that which God hath intended in His Book, for in truth He knoweth that which is enshrined in the Bayan by virtue of the Will of Him Who is the Omnipotent, the Powerful.

order.why: Retain the call for fair judgment of the Most Great Remembrance.
Ask how remembrance becomes possible through prior divine remembrance.
shortened: The remembrance of God is a leaf among His leaves, and verily His remembrance hath preceded all worlds. Were it not for His remembrance, none would have known Him to remember Him.

order.why: Read the invitation to turn toward the living Remembrance.
Hear the prayer’s relation between self, praise, and remembrance.
shortened: I am carried back to such heights that I recognize my self to be the same as the remembrance of Thee in Thy realm, and the essence of Thy praise among Thy servants. As long as that self endureth, so long will Thy praise continue to be shed abroad among Thy creatures and Thy remembrance glorified by Thy people.

order.why: Consider the prayer’s description of the Revealer and its request for direction.
Retain the brief petition for aid to the divine Remembrance.
shortened: If Thou refusest, O my God, to aid them that love Thee, assist Thou, then, Thine own Self and Him Who is Thy Remembrance.

order.why: Read the petition to be quickened through the Word.
shortened: I implore Thee, by this very word that hath shone forth above the horizon of Thy will, to enable me to drink deep of the living waters through which Thou hast vivified the hearts of Thy chosen ones and quickened the souls of them that love Thee, that I may, at all times and under all conditions, turn my face wholly towards Thee.

order.why: Consider divine mention as a lamp before the soul.
shortened: God willing, may all attain unto the eternal bounty which in one instance hath been interpreted as the Divine Word. This exalted Word hath been recorded by the Most Exalted Pen in the Crimson Book: "Blessed is the soul that hath attained unto the Word of God in His days," for whosoever attaineth unto divine mention, that mention appeareth as a lamp before his face, manifest, evident, bright and visible in all the worlds.

order.why: Connect recognition with detachment from covetousness and unseemly conduct.
shortened: Purify yourselves with the water of detachment from covetousness and unseemly deeds, that ye may discover the mystery of the Day of the Self-Subsisting. The Primal Light hath appeared in the Final Day.

order.why: Read continuing instruction according to the capacity of those taught.
Consider differing forms and stations of divine command.
Keep the particular image of entrusted reins within its source’s decree.
Hear the question concerning signs, command, and power.
Read the world kindled by the Tree of Command.
shortened: The world hath been set ablaze by the Fire that hath been kindled from the Tree of God's Command, the Lord of all worlds.

order.why: Consider the narrative image of love’s fire and the revealed Word.
shortened: Then another countenance emerged and said: "Verily it is the fire of the love of God, and when it appeared on the Mount of Beauty, the Most Exalted Word was revealed in the form 'There is no God but Me, the Powerful, the Imprisoned.'"

order.why: Close the linked readings with the declared purpose of bringing life.
Read the supplied distinction among God, Word, and created things with its attributed authority.
shortened: ...the gnostics maintain the existence of only two worlds, the world of God and the world of the creature. The prophets, however, maintained the existence of three worlds: the world of God, the world of the Will or the Word, and the world of created things. The Prophets, therefore, maintained that a knowledge of God is impossible.... There is, therefore, only one way to God and that is through the realization of His Manifestation or Prophet in that age.

order.why: Retain the provisional summary relating Manifestations to the Primal Will.
Explore the supplied sun analogy for the unity of successive Manifestations.
shortened: ...the First Remembrance, which is the Primal Will of God, may be likened unto the sun.

And know thou that He indeed resembleth the sun. Were the risings of the sun to continue till the end that hath no end, yet there hath not been nor ever will be more than one sun.... It is this Primal Will which appeareth resplendent in every Prophet and speaketh forth in every revealed Book.

order.why: Read the supplied provisional image of the Point as mirror.
Consider the Bayan as the unfolding of the Point in this provisional rendering.
Retain the related provisional account of differentiation into letters.
Read the provisional account of light and fire through the Point.
Explore the supplied provisional account of the seven modes without filling its omissions.
shortened: God in truth created the Will before all other things and made it the cause of their existence. It is the First Remembrance, whereof the Imam asked while addressing Jonah: "Dost thou know what the Will is?" He replied: "No." Then he explained: "It is the First Remembrance." Through the gift of His wisdom and the excellence of His craftsmanship, God placed within it a sign of the manifestation of His self-subsistence, that it might indicate His oneness under all conditions. This Will hath seven modes without which it is impossible for anything to be clothed in the vesture of existence...

order.why: Consider the supplied qualification of a philosophical maxim about the One.
shortened: Concerning thy question about the meaning of the philosopher's saying, "From the One proceedeth only One": The statement is incorrect when the Cause is meant to be the Absolute Essence... However, when the intention behind the statement is to refer to the Primal Utterance, which is created by God by Itself, for Itself, then verily it is the truth...

There is no doubt that the Eternal Essence hath ever been immeasurably exalted above any association with His creatures; how much less could it become the source out of which things proceed. Though the statement is discussed in philosophy, the truth is that it must refer to the grades of the creative Action itself.

order.why: Keep the provisional account of four causes and elements in its metaphysical context.
Read the supplied scholarly comparison with Sufism and Plotinus as an interpretation.
Retain the supplied historical account of the Bab’s titles.
Read the supplied address concerning the Most Great Remembrance.
End with the stated purpose of signs in scripture, world, and heart.

questions: How does a Word without syllable or sound challenge familiar assumptions about language and meaning?
What can the images of sun and mirror, point and letters, and a complete word illuminate—and what remains beyond them?
How do these selections distinguish knowing the Manifestation from comprehending the divine Essence?
What becomes clearer when John 1:1–18 is read alongside the interpretations of Christ and the Word included here?
How might recognition of the Word be reflected in education, fellowship, and the overcoming of hostility?
Which connected subject would help you explore further the relation among divine Will, the Holy Spirit, and human response?

references.label: 1 · John 1:1–18 · Word, life, light, and revelation
references.note: Read the Gospel’s opening account of the Word, creation, light, and revelation in Jesus Christ beside the interpretations quoted in this guide. The comparison invites close attention to both the Gospel’s own claims and the Baha’i use of the mirror and divine-perfections imagery; it does not assume all Christian and Baha’i interpretations are identical.

subjects.displayTitle: Striving: discovering a path and walking it
subjects.introduction: Discovering the way to America, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá once remarked, does not bring anyone to America; a road has to be travelled. Effort in the Bahá’í writings is this second act, the turning of understanding into movement, and its field is as wide as a life: daily work done with trust in God, conduct that grows a little more beautiful each day, knowledge and craft acquired according to one’s means, and the long emigration out of the realm of self toward the heart of the Friend. Capacity, He says, follows striving and sincerity. The urgency is real, since no one can count on another moment of life, yet it is softened by counsel to be patient when results are slow and to let obstacles become steps. Guidance itself remains a gift, and the Qur’anic promise that those who strive in God’s path will be guided to His ways holds the two together [1]. The journey continues through the condition of search, through steadfastness and perseverance, and along the spiritual path itself.
subjects.arc: Begin by distinguishing knowing the way from walking it, join effort to service and grace, then explore patient learning, urgency, and the fruits of sustained action.

order.why: Place human faculties in service of the general good.
Open with the difference between discovering a road and traveling it.
shortened: It is not sufficient only to distinguish the way of the Kingdom, only to discover the heavenly way: you must travel upon it until the end is reached. For example, that a man discovers the way to America is not sufficient. He must travel in it that he may reach that country.

order.why: Pair determined work with trust in God.
shortened: However, the cause of success and prosperity is trustworthiness and religiosity and effort and zeal, and conduct and movement according to divine teachings. Strive in your work but trust in God. Seek assistance and grace from Him, and seek success and prosperity and advancement from Him.

order.why: Define daily progress through conduct, forbearance, and love.
shortened: Therefore, we must strive with life and heart that, day by day, our deeds may be better, our conduct more beautiful and our forbearance greater. That is, to cultivate love for all the world; to attain beatific character.

order.why: Connect knowledge and craft with effort according to capacity and means.
shortened: Strive diligently to acquire both outward and inward perfections, for the fruit of the human tree has ever been outer and inner perfections. A person without knowledge and crafts is not beloved - like trees without fruit have they been and ever shall be. Therefore you must needs adorn, according to your capacity and means, the tree of your being with the fruits of knowledge and wisdom, of meanings and utterance.

order.why: Distinguish moral excellence from wealth and outward status.
shortened: I desire distinction for you. The Baha'is must be distinguished from others of humanity. But this distinction must not depend upon wealth -- that they should become more affluent than other people. I do not desire for you financial distinction. It is not an ordinary distinction I desire; not scientific, commercial, industrial distinction. For you I desire spiritual distinction -- that is, you must become eminent and distinguished in morals.

order.why: Consider guidance as a gift alongside the fruits of endeavor.
shortened: In the world of existence, every gift can be attained through effort and endeavor, through seeking and yearning, but guidance is a divine bestowal and a heavenly gift.

order.why: Read striving with meditation and the cited Quranic promise.
shortened: Today striving is necessary, and likewise meditation on the signs in the horizons and within yourselves. His exalted Word: "And those who strive in Our path, We shall assuredly guide them to Our ways."

order.why: Consider taking practical means while trusting divine provision.
Read the school’s establishment through zeal, patience, and pure intention.
Attend to intention and patient expectation beyond initial appearances.
shortened: One must not look to the beginning of matters - one must strive in affairs with pure intention and ultimately await the results.

order.why: Retain the particular counsel to endure and be patient.
Read the reported gardener and traveler as images of perseverance.
Consider the reported value of completing a task once begun.
Read the reported pupil’s persistence in learning.
Retain the related reported call to search and learn.
Consider the reported cultivation of existing abilities.
Read striving in relation to sincerity.
shortened: Capacity is in accordance with striving and sincerity.

order.why: Consider becoming receptive to grace through effort.
Read daily growth in capacity and certitude.
shortened: Strive night and day that capacity, worthiness and merit may increase, and advance day by day in the degrees of recognition and certitude, so that you may be counted among the friends of the Most Glorious Beauty and the loved ones of the Most Exalted Lord.

order.why: Keep the reported possibility of further advancement at every level.
shortened: No matter what level a human being reaches, he can still attain higher ones, so he is always making effort and desiring more.

order.why: Read the reported need to fulfill a task’s conditions.
Consider a specific encouragement to develop writing and speech in cooperation.
Read effort directed toward understanding the symbols of scripture.
shortened: O thou who art advancing toward God!

Verily, I read thy long letter, which showed thine abundant joy for the appearance of the Kingdom of God and longing of thy heart for the knowledge of God. Endeavor with thy soul, so that the fountain of knowledge may flow within thy heart and the bounties of mysteries may pour upon thee from the Kingdom of Lights. Then thou wilt understand the meanings hidden and recorded in the symbols in the Holy Scriptures.

order.why: Consider the reported call to reflect upon hardship before beginning the journey.
