shortened: First must we meditate upon it and consider the hardships, trials, and calamities, then must we resolve and commence our journey. We witness how people sacrifice their wealth and much else to discover the North Pole, with great devotion. How much greater must our devotion be in seeking the Pole of the Kingdom!

order.why: Distinguish ease from the reported independence won through meaningful effort.
shortened: Even a little bird perched upon the loftiest branch of a tree on a hill-top commands a view and occupies a height that Kings might envy. He has no troubles or trials. But such freedom and loftiness are of no consequence; while a man who endures trials, and sacrifices ease and comfort to great achievements, is endowed with true independence.

order.why: Keep the North Pole example and its historical claim within the reported address.
shortened: Confirmation is not dependent on talent, knowledge or wisdom. Many unimportant persons have made significant discoveries. Many people labored for years to explore the North Pole but Admiral Peary reached it. One's efforts should be focussed on the object of one's quest.

order.why: Read the related reported comparison of costly exploration with spiritual pursuit.
shortened: All the difficulties and hardships which they endured! How many ships were wrecked, how many souls were lost, how much property was destroyed until they could discover the North Pole! Finally they found it, and it was nothing.

order.why: Hear the reported encouragement to continue beyond delayed results.
shortened: Once his effort is directed in the proper channel if he does not succeed today he will succeed tomorrow. Effort in itself is one of the noblest traits of human character.

order.why: Consider the reported image of obstacles becoming steps.
shortened: A third class of men and women to whom nature has bestowed an iron will, an adamant determination, an unwavering strength, a sterling character, a dominating personality, a passionate desire in doing good,- look upon all hindrances and stumbling-blocks as so many ladders or stepping-stones to rise and rise till they have grasped into their mighty hands the scepter of glory.

order.why: Read enthusiasm in relation to proficiency and weariness.
Hear the reported emphasis on joyful activity.
shortened: Not through idleness do we accomplish anything but through ceaseless, joyful, ever expanding activity.

order.why: Consider the reported conjunction of humility, thoughtfulness, and active service.
shortened: In this court we must be humble and meek, active and progressive, wide-awake and thoughtful, true and sincere, noble and good, straightforward and zealous.
This is the outcome of life! This is the result of ceaseless endeavour!

order.why: Read the images of spreading wings and learning to swim.
shortened: It is time to surge like the ocean and soar to the Pleiades. If we seek to ascend to the highest horizon we must spread our wings, and if we wish to dive into the ocean's depths we must learn to swim.

order.why: Connect desire, humility, bodily effort, and spiritual aspiration.
shortened: Therefore, desire with your heart and demonstrate humility and lowliness with your soul, show forth the strength of your arms with your body, and strive with all your powers until this brilliant star of bounty may rise from the horizon of heart and soul, and this bird of aspiration may fall into the snare of attainment, this flower may bloom in the gathering, and this dove may sing in that garden.

order.why: Read the whole person’s participation in seeking.
Consider effort as movement beyond self and desire.
shortened: But effort is needed until thou emigratest from the realm of self and desire and soarest to the sacred precincts of holiness and becomest intimate with the sanctuary of the soul and findest the way to the heart of the Friend. How sweet is this utterance and how excellent must be the deed! If thou hearkenest to the counsel of the Friend and journeyest in the paths of His good-pleasure - keep far from thyself and draw near to thy Lord; cast away what thy self desireth and seek what thy Lord willeth; forget all else and remember His light.

order.why: Hear the warning against deprivation of the portion of striving.
shortened: Deprive not thyself of the portion of striving, for hearts become ill just as bodies become ill. Therefore, purify thy heart through remembrance of God the Most Great in every condition.

order.why: Read the reported image of inexhaustible thirst.
Consider the reported fountain that must be sought.
Hear the invitation to receive from the ocean and fields of grace.
Read the pursuit of gifts glimpsed in the degrees of existence.
Keep the personal address concerning stations and seeking.
shortened: O 'Ali! God has ordained stations for His loved ones in all ranks and conditions, and has called them to striving and seeking that He might bestow upon them that which they desire.

order.why: Read opportunity for receiving bounty amid divine confirmation.
Consider effort directed toward recognition.
Retain the related appeal to attain what has been set forth.
shortened: O ye who soar in the atmosphere of divine recognition! Make a mighty effort that ye may attain unto that which hath been mentioned.

order.why: Read aspiration toward lofty stations.
shortened: God willing, may they fix their gaze upon lofty stations and strive with the utmost effort and endeavor to attain them.

order.why: Hear the invitation to seek the fragrances of eternity.
shortened: Say: O friends! Man hath been created for this blessed and wondrous Day. Strive ye that ye may attain unto that wherefrom the fragrances of eternity are wafted.

order.why: Consider effort made recognizable through the fragrance of love.
shortened: Strive thou that there may appear from thee that from which the sincere ones may inhale the fragrance of the love of God, the Goal of all who have recognized Him.

order.why: Calls for the fullest effort and appropriate means in every undertaking.
Read the image of becoming enkindled by divine radiance.
Connect increasing effort with deepening love and nearness.
shortened: Increase also thine efforts, and day by day settle more in the Kingdom, and be nearer to God, till Love may surge within thee every minute, and may take thee to whatever is the desire of the near ones.

order.why: Retain the reported encouragement toward brighter love and stronger service.
Read the aspiration to continuous remembrance and service.
Join increasing hope with continued effort.
Consider effort, bounty, ascent, and progress together.
shortened: The more effort is expended, the more bounty will be received, and the more one ascends, the more progress will be achieved in all directions.

order.why: Read the seed and abundant harvest while preserving its source omission.
shortened: Know thou that this effort was like the sowing of a seed that shall yield a bountiful harvest. As mentioned in the Qur'an: "like a grain which groweth seven ears, in every ear a hundred grains" - so shall it be. Ere long, praiseworthy results and acceptable effects of this deed shall become evident and manifest....

order.why: Consider endeavor moving toward fruit and renewed joyful worship.
shortened: So now you must strive until the result is achieved and the fruit obtained and the lamp of eternal life is kindled and the gifts of the Lord of the Kingdom become manifest, and again engage in worship of the Lord of Hosts with utmost joy and delight.

order.why: Read the strong appeal to determination within its account of human possibility.
shortened: A few souls, unaware of the power latent in human endeavor, consider this matter as highly impracticable, nay even beyond the scope of man's utmost efforts. Such is not the case, however. On the contrary, thanks to the unfailing grace of God, the loving-kindness of His favored ones, the unrivaled endeavors of wise and capable souls, and the thoughts and ideas of the peerless leaders of this age, nothing whatsoever can be regarded as unattainable.
Endeavor, ceaseless endeavor, is required. Nothing short of an indomitable determination can possibly achieve it.

order.why: Turn toward the collective transformation sought by effort.
shortened: O ye true friends! Make ye a mighty effort, that this world may become another world, and this darksome earth may become shining and resplendent through the rays of the Sun of Truth.
I entreat God that this favor may be realized and this unending outpouring become manifest and apparent, and the friends of God be confirmed by every bounty.

order.why: Consider the images of humanity as one tree and one ocean.
Read striving as living by divine counsels and united joyful service.
shortened: O ye two lovers of the Beauty of ABHA! Ere long the Word of God will display a wonderful influence and finally that region (America) will become the paradise of ABHA. Consequently, strive ye bravely that this aim may be accomplished in the near future. Striving means this: Ye must live and move according to the divine commands and behests, be united in loving with ecstasy and joy; do not take any rest but engage continually in the service of the Cause of God.

order.why: Keep intense exhortation and the appeal for divine assistance together.
shortened: Indulge not your bodies with rest, but work with all your souls, and with all your hearts cry out and beg of God to grant you His succor and grace. Thus may ye make this world the Abha Paradise, and this globe of earth the parade ground of the realm on high. If only ye exert the effort, it is certain that these splendors will shine out, these clouds of mercy will shed down their rain, these life-giving winds will rise and blow, this sweet-smelling musk will be scattered far and wide.

order.why: Read the call to labor in response to Baha’u’llah’s suffering.
shortened: Now is the time, O ye beloved of the Lord, for ardent endeavour. Struggle ye, and strive. And since the Ancient Beauty was exposed by day and night on the field of martyrdom, let us in our turn labour hard, and hear and ponder the counsels of God; let us fling away our lives, and renounce our brief and numbered days.

order.why: Consider the urgency of finite life and the danger of postponement.
shortened: Expend your every breath of life in this great Cause and dedicate all your days to the service of Baha, so that in the end, safe from loss and deprivation, ye will inherit the heaped-up treasures of the realms above. For the days of a man are full of peril and he cannot rely on so much as a moment more of life; and still the people, who are even as a wavering mirage of illusions, tell themselves that in the end they shall reach the heights.

order.why: Read the lamp’s remaining oil as an image of present opportunity.
shortened: While there is still oil in thy lamp, therefore, while there is yet some strength left in thy body, make thou a mighty effort that thy faith may burn brightly within the globe of divine grace and bounty.

order.why: Hear the counsel not to let time and beneficence escape.
Read the sharp image of time and a fleeting opportunity.
Consider directing effort toward what bears fruit.
Keep the uncompromising exhortation against negligence in its own voice.
shortened: Yes, striving and endeavor, effort and exertion are necessary and obligatory, while negligence and laxity are blameworthy and reproachable. Indeed, one must not be idle for a moment day and night, nor let a minute slip away.

order.why: Read the description of consecrated service through its devotional intensity.
shortened: These shall labour ceaselessly, by day and by night, shall heed neither trials nor woe, shall suffer no respite in their efforts, shall seek no repose, shall disregard all ease and comfort, and, detached and unsullied, shall consecrate every fleeting moment of their lives to the diffusion of the divine fragrance and the exaltation of God's holy Word.

order.why: Retain the brief appeal to unremitting effort.
shortened: Loose thy tongue and teach, and let thy face be bright with the fire of God's love. Rest thou not for a moment, seek thou to draw no easeful breath. Thus mayest thou become a sign and symbol of God's love, and a banner of His grace.

order.why: Consider the artery’s pulsation as an image of life-giving activity.
Hear the invitation to diligent work for enduring bounty.
Preserve the source’s wording in its particular call to determination.
Read the aspiration to a new age of unity.
shortened: In this age of grace, make a boundless effort and endeavor, that thou mayest become sanctified above the signs of past ages and become a brilliant moon among the renowned ones of the age of unity.

order.why: Consider the appeal to excellence in purity, refinement, knowledge, and self-control.
Enter the image of the arena and the dispelling of doubt.
shortened: This is the day of the arena and the time of polo mallet and ball. Make an effort to snatch away this ball of precedence and victory, to utterly rout the armies of doubts and dispel the darkness of uncertainty.

order.why: Retain the related images of endeavor and pursuit.
shortened: Effort and endeavor are needed, zeal and enthusiasm are required, and in this arena, striving is necessary and hunting is obligatory.

order.why: Keep the polo-field exhortation in its original form.
shortened: Be like men and cast your ball into the field. I hope you will be a man of the field, wielding the polo stick and seizing the ball.

order.why: Read the congratulatory use of the same sporting image.
Consider gratitude as the motive for striving.
shortened: Therefore night and day we must strive and endeavor that perchance in gratitude for the favors of the one true God we may draw breath and make the world a companion to this abundant grace.

order.why: Hear the appeal for confirmation and assistance.
shortened: Otherwise, "if He forsake you, who is there that can help you after Him?" will become manifest and apparent. Therefore, strive that thou mayest be confirmed and assisted.

order.why: Read the reported relation between effort and spiritual attainment.
Consider the reported purpose of awakening perception.
Keep the numerical contrast about transformation within the reported statement.
Read the reported praise of prompt attendance to duties in its particular setting.
Turn to the supplied counsel about excellence in arts and skills.
End with the supplied call to better one another’s lives.

questions: What is the difference between recognizing a worthwhile path and beginning to travel it?
How might effort according to one’s capacity be both demanding and sustainable?
What changes when striving is directed toward better conduct and the good of others rather than personal distinction?
How does Qur’an 29:69 help you think about the relationship among effort, guidance, and doing good?
What roles do patience, enthusiasm, cooperation, and trust play when results are slow to appear?
Which practical commitment could turn an aspiration into a continuing habit of learning and service?

references.label: 1 · Qur’an 29:69 · Striving, guidance, and goodness
references.note: Read Pickthall’s translation alongside the parallel renderings on this page. The verse joins striving with divine guidance and God’s presence with those who do good. Compare it with the compilation’s own citation of this verse and with the passages that distinguish human effort from the gift of guidance.

subjects.displayTitle: The Promised One: when expectation becomes encounter
subjects.introduction: Devotion to a promise can harden into the very thing that hides its fulfilment. The Báb planted the Bayan, He says, for no purpose but that His followers might recognize the One He called Him Whom God shall make manifest, and He warned them that no allusion of His own, no treasure of gold or height of piety, would suffice in the Day of that encounter; they were to take fresh sustenance from what would then be sent down, and to grieve no soul, lest they wound Him unawares. Bahá’u’lláh declared Himself that promised One, affirming at the same time the Báb’s full station as a Manifestation of God and likening their bond to that of John the Baptist and Jesus. John’s own words about the bridegroom’s friend, glad to hear his voice and content to decrease [1], give the comparison its tenderness. Recognition, seen this way, is less a conclusion than a readiness: a heart that fixes its gaze, prays to be among the believers, and counts its hours of meeting as its best. The journey continues toward the Báb Himself and His claims, toward Bahá’u’lláh, toward the pattern of prophecy and fulfilment, and toward the laws of the Bayan and their passing.
subjects.arc: Begin with the danger of becoming veiled by one’s own expectation, examine the Bayan’s purpose and the herald relationship, then follow recognition into prayer, conduct, and an open future.

order.why: Read the planting of the Bayan through its intended fruit of recognition.
shortened: Indeed My aim in planting the Tree of the Bayan hath been none other than to enable you to recognize Me. In truth I Myself am the first to bow down before God and to believe in Him. Therefore let not your recognition become fruitless, inasmuch as the Bayan, notwithstanding the sublimity of its station, beareth fealty to Him Whom God shall make manifest, and it is He Who beseemeth most to be acclaimed as the Seat of divine Reality, though indeed He is I and I am He.

order.why: Open with the invitation to examine oneself as one examines earlier religious communities.
Consider receiving new sustenance rather than relying only on what was received before.
Read the extensive glad tidings, warnings, and appeal not to grieve any soul.
shortened: Say: Verily God giveth you glad tidings of Him Whom God shall make manifest - will ye not rejoice? Say: Verily God giveth you glad tidings of the glory of Him Whom God shall make manifest - will ye not rejoice? Say: Verily God giveth you glad tidings of the beauty of Him Whom God shall make manifest - will ye not rejoice?

Therefore fear God, O all things, from the Day of Him Whom God shall make manifest, for ye know not whether this is He Whom God shall make manifest. Nay, even should He make Himself known unto you after His manifestation, then would ye hear and know. Therefore have mercy upon yourselves, that ye transgress not the bounds of the Bayan, and grieve not any soul, that this may return unto Him Whom God shall make manifest while ye know not.

order.why: Consider the Bayan’s own account of its relation to the coming Revelation.
shortened: O ye the created beings of the Bayan! We verily have made you recognize the uttermost excellence of your existence which lieth in the word of your Lord, that ye may not be veiled from Him Whom God shall assuredly make manifest, in truth, in the Day of Resurrection. For verily all that ye speak is a mere image of His revealed word within your hearts, whereas that which He proclaimeth is what God hath testified unto Himself, that, "verily there is none other God but Him, the Omnipotent, the Self-Subsisting."

order.why: Establish the distinct stations affirmed for the Bab and Baha’u’llah.
shortened: This is the foundation of the belief of the people of Baha (may my life be offered up for them): "His Holiness, the Exalted One (the Bab), is the Manifestation of the Unity and Oneness of God and the Forerunner of the Ancient Beauty. His Holiness the Abha Beauty (may my life be a sacrifice for His steadfast friends) is the Supreme Manifestation of God and the Dayspring of His Most Divine Essence. All others are servants unto Him and do His bidding."

order.why: Keep the particular account of Emmanuel as a herald in its source’s terms.
Introduce the image of John proclaiming in the wilderness of the Bayan.
Read the account of the Bab’s educational influence and preparation of His followers.
shortened: The government, the nation, the clergy, and prominent leaders sought to extinguish His light, but to no avail. At last His moon rose, His star shone forth, His foundation was secured, and His horizon was flooded with light. He trained a large multitude through divine education and exerted a marvellous influence upon the thoughts, customs, morals, and manners of the Persians. He proclaimed the glad-tidings of the manifestation of the Sun of Baha to all His followers and readied them for faith and certitude.

order.why: Consider the Book’s address to Him Whom God shall make manifest.
shortened: Say: This is the Book from God, the Help in Peril, the Self-Subsisting, unto Him Whom God shall make manifest. Bear thou witness that there is no God but Me, the Mighty, the Well-Beloved. I have created all things, both before and after, that they may believe in Thee on the day of Thy manifestation, and in Thy signs, that they may be among the guided ones.

order.why: Contrasts recognition and denial of Him Whom God shall make manifest.
Read successive revelation as preparation for a subsequent Manifestation.
shortened: Thou hast never sent a Messenger, nor revealed a Book, nor supported the people of the religion of God except for Him Whom Thou shalt manifest on the Day of Resurrection through Thy signs. Verily, Thou hast never revealed any decree in any Manifestation except that Thou didst intend to exalt the Manifestation of Thyself in the subsequent Revelation.

order.why: Retain the striking repeated anticipation of further divine manifestations.
Consider the warning against becoming veiled by the Bab and the Letters of the Living.
shortened: He states that in the Manifestation of "Him Whom God shall make manifest" you should not be veiled by the Vahid of the Bayan - and the Vahid of the Bayan refers to the Bab Himself and the eighteen Letters of the Living. Similarly He states not to be veiled by what was revealed in the Bayan.

order.why: Read the related interpretation of barriers removed and commandments made conditional.
shortened: Praise be to God that the Exalted One, may my spirit be sacrificed for Him, left no veil and demolished the barriers. The entire Bayan openly points to Him Whom God shall make manifest, and all matters are conditional upon and dependent on the confirmation of that Pure Being. He says: 'Beware, beware lest thou be veiled by the Vahid of the Bayan, for it is as creation before Him. Beware, beware lest thou be veiled by what was revealed in the Bayan.'

order.why: Examine the challenge of recognizing beyond the Bayan’s allusions.
shortened: The Exalted One - may the spirit of all who are in the kingdom of Command and Creation be a sacrifice unto Him - proclaims with the most elevated call, His word, exalted and mighty: "I have written a gem concerning His remembrance: He shall not be known through My allusions, nor through what is mentioned in the Bayan." Do the people of the Bayan consider these words, which flowed from the lips of the Primal Point's Will - may the spirit of all else be a sacrifice unto Him - to be false or true? If, God forbid, they deem it false, then no further word remains. And if they accept it as true, what then are these words and these objections?

order.why: Read the Kitab-i-Badi’s account of the Bayan’s purpose within its polemical setting.
shortened: He arose not but to mention Him, retired not but to praise Him, moved not but in love of Him, and breathed not but in His Cause, while ye turned away from Him and objected to Him, clinging to one who is more contemptible in God's sight than yourselves, did ye but know it. Ye have turned away from the Beloved of all creation, concerning Whom the Point of the Bayan hath said, exalted be His mention: 'Were it not for His Book, this Book would not have been revealed, and were it not for His Self, God would not have manifested Me.'

order.why: Consider the anniversary commemoration’s statement of that purpose.
Keep the emphatic claim and its historical rebuke in the source’s own voice.
shortened: Naught was revealed in the Bayan save mention of Me, and all that was ordained therein was held within the grasp of My power, as attesteth all that was sent down aforetime unto 'Ali from One mighty and beauteous. Say: Woe unto you, O concourse of idolaters! Ye have denied Him but for Whom the Bayan would not have been revealed, nor would 'Ali have appeared with the truth, nor would the heavens and earths have been created. Say: His purpose was none other than My Self and the dawning of My Manifestation from this luminous and resplendent horizon.

order.why: Read the related declaration concerning the Bayan’s appearance.
Hear the appeal to fair-mindedness concerning the Primal Point’s testimony.
Consider the statement about the priority of the Covenant.
shortened: By God! The Primal Point took the Covenant of My Being before His own Covenant, and was speaking in My Name and heralding My Revelation and was submissive unto My firm and mighty Command.

order.why: Read the relation between sacrifice and the anticipated manifestation.
shortened: He is the One for Whose sake Thou (the Bab) hast yielded Thy life, and hast consented to be touched by the manifold ills of the world that He may manifest Himself, and summoned all mankind in His name.

order.why: Return to the image of the herald’s proclamation.
shortened: He proclaimed in the wilderness of the Bayan and gave you glad tidings of your Lord, the All-Merciful. Then He came with mighty sovereignty. He testified of Me and informed you of My kingdom and dominion.

order.why: Read the declaration of the Primal Point’s purpose and continuing testimony.
Consider the claim of the Primal Point’s renewed appearance.
shortened: O handmaiden of God! Hearken unto the call of thy Lord from this holy and blessed quarter, that there is none other God but Him, and that He Who speaketh at this moment is indeed the Primal Point, Who hath appeared once again - whereat all witnesses and the witnessed were thunderstruck, save those who had quaffed the water of life, and these were but a numbered few.

order.why: Retain the reported announcement identifying Baha’u’llah with the Promised One.
shortened: We announce to you Baha'u'llah, "He whom God shall manifest," the one who has broken the seals of both the creational and collective books.

order.why: Keep the reported chronology and secret-correspondence claim in its attribution.
Read the particular account of meetings and glad tidings in its source’s terms.
Retain the reported account of spiritual communication.
shortened: Those souls who are believers in God and are assured of the Blessed Beauty and the Bab - to them the truth of the Blessed Beauty and the Bab is as clear as the sun. These souls know that between the Blessed Beauty and the Bab there was spiritual communication that continued without interruption.

subjects.displayTitle: A name and its bearer: remembrance, hope, and character
subjects.introduction: A name, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá wrote to a believer who asked about changing his, has no importance of its own, for a name must have a bearer who deserves it. A man may carry the name of a bright star and still sit in darkness, while one whose name is obscure may shine like the morning. That thread runs through every naming He bestowed: a child called Beauty is prayed for so that she may become beautiful in all conditions, a man named Bahram or Abbas is told that the star or the lion must now show itself in his deeds, and a daughter named for the Sun is given with the hope that all around her become lamps. Names also carry memory, of a grandfather, a late grandmother, an old friend, a martyr. Luke’s account of the naming of John, where family custom meets a different calling, offers a kindred scene [1]. Reading each of these personal instructions with its own recipient in view opens the larger question of how a life gives substance to what it is called.
subjects.arc: Begin with character giving a name its substance, explore prayer and family remembrance, then read the varied personal bestowals as expressions of hope, service, and gratitude.

shortened: A name hath no importance, for a name must needs have a bearer (i. e., deserving a high name). That is to say, consider (people's) morals and character, then consider the person himself and be attentive (to detect) one's manners and conduct and consider his faith and assurance. If a person is illumined with the light of the love of God, he is (like unto) the morning star, even though his name be dark; and if he is a captive in the darkness of error, he is gloomy even though his name be that of a shining star.
